'Mice' is the plural of 'mouse'..why: True by English morphology: 'mice' is the standard irregular plural of 'mouse'.

'Mice' is the plural of 'moose'..why: Deliberately false side fact for the disjunction: the plural of 'moose' is normally 'moose', and 'mice' is the plural of 'mouse'.

sources.quote: The form meese is sometimes also used humorously as the plural of moose—normally moose or mooses—or even of mouse.

'Is sedge-filed under' is asymmetric..why: 'Sedge-filed under' is a made-up relation (catalogued as sedge_filed_under, fictional, with no property tags): Wikipedia and Dolma have no such phrase, and 'filed under' reads one way (a thing is filed under a heading), so a model's default reading of it is one-way already; the record's prompts state the premise and ask what the inserted property gives, and the pre-edit audit must confirm that models do not already answer 'no' to the converse question. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

notes: Dev RBox expansion, fictional relation with real word instances, paired with the revision grammar-replace-d006 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'). The revision changes 'rhymes with' from symmetric to asymmetric; this insert gives the made-up relation sedge_filed_under the revision's new property, asymmetry, so revision and expansion send the model to the same property (changed after review from symmetry, the revision's old property, which made the pair test opposite properties). The instances mirror the revision's: the first asks whether the converse follows (no after the edit), the second whether the converse's negation follows (yes), which also balances yes and no. Spec note, recorded: the README says asymmetry is not used in derived queries because an asymmetry 'no' is usually the same before and after; for a made-up relation the answer before the edit is null (nothing is known), so the answers do change, and the revision grammar-replace-d006 itself uses asymmetry. Residual risk, recorded: 'filed under' reads one way, so a model may answer 'no' to the converse without the edit; the pre-edit audit has to show the models do not already answer 'no'. The word pairs (lantern/harbor, velvet/thunder) carry no stored link the coined relation could borrow, and the premise is given in the prompt. Near unrelated asks the same property of a real grammar relation whose answer is 'no' (synonym_of is not asymmetric, the same question the revision asks), so an edit that spreads asymmetry to other word relations is caught; far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. The cross-lingual prompts keep the coined term untranslated inside a full sentence frame. hops counts the prompt's premise as the bridge, as the other RBox records do. Made-up term: Dolma has 0 hits for 'sedge-filed', 'sedge-filed under' and 'sedge filed under', and Wikipedia search finds nothing (2026-11-12).
